layout.title: Broader coverage changes the findings
layout.notes: The expanded study was finalized on 14 October 2026 Asia/Jakarta. Cohort/run folders retain the 20261013 preparation identifier. All 40 model/cohort/split summaries completed, with 55,156 new predictions. Inputs are protocol evaluations, not independent events: windows share frame endpoints, and person/loitering queries share images. No additional latency experiment was run. MiniCPM has the highest raw unattended frame-test F1, but only 34.7% recall. The new event labels are provisional assistant timeline review, without independent human verification. The other three requested anomalies were attempted as explicitly limited diagnostics. Smoking and supervised offline VadCLIP evidence are reused, not rerun.

layout.title: Use the available data at its valid level
layout.notes: The unattended frames and 20-second windows each have 808 dev and 962 test inputs. Both protocols share 1,770 endpoints. Littering contributes 6,667 unique decoded images after removing 17 aliases from the usable collector rows; augmentations remain and are not independent source events. Loitering and person-presence are different queries on the same 1,675 person-labelled images. Rough sleeping uses 111 full synthetic lying/fall scenes as weak candidates. The oracle pose diagnostic uses 121 box crops from the same pose source, split by original image into 73 dev and 48 test crops. The prior smoking study already uses 3,278 local development frames and is retained separately.

layout.title: Recover events from source timelines
layout.notes: Source videos were reviewed chronologically and event/control intervals were chosen before the new inference. CAVIAR XML roles supplement visual timeline evidence, rather than equating an object box with abandonment. Frames are lossless native-resolution PNGs at actual source frame indices, sampled approximately 2 fps; source SHA, frame index and timestamps are saved. The 18 included recordings comprise eight CAVIAR and ten ABODA recordings, contributing event intervals and/or clear controls. Exact duplicate raw/additional video copies are not counted twice. Behind-chair occlusion, owners remaining nearby, occluded ABODA placements and a pre-existing item without owner history are excluded as positives. This is assistant-generated provisional annotation, not independent human ground truth.

layout.title: Related camera recordings stay together
layout.notes: Development uses CAVIAR's INRIA camera, ABODA lobby and ABODA entrance families: 808 endpoints, 255 positive and 553 normal. Test uses the ABODA walkway and classroom families: 962 endpoints, 242 positive and 720 normal, seven recordings, five positive source intervals. Related classroom views are conservatively held together. The camera/source clusters, rather than adjacent frame samples, are the bootstrap unit. There are only two test families, so uncertainty estimates are exploratory and cannot establish broad camera generalization. CLIP thresholds are chosen from development and applied unchanged to test. All weak exports remain development-only because event labels and/or source identities are insufficient. Source-image identities keep all pose crops from one original image in the same split.

layout.title: Run quality evaluation without pacing
layout.notes: All four models ran on the RTX 5000 Ada with CUDA. Accuracy was unpaced, without a default host RAM cap. The four model workers ran concurrently with eight CPU threads each. CLIP inference used batch 64, float32 weights; generative models used single-input calls and unquantized bfloat16 weights. The shared input policy letterboxes and bounds the image to 768 pixels before native model processing. Generation is deterministic with max_new_tokens 64. MiniCPM keeps the previous one-slice configuration. There is one measured prediction per input, no latency repetitions and no warmup calls; this is a quality experiment. Four-frame 2×2 contact sheets use only past context over 20 seconds, versus six seconds in the earlier study. This is not each model's native multi-frame video API, and sheets reduce spatial detail per frame. Exact commands, revisions and raw responses are saved.

layout.title: Keep event quality and diagnostics separate
layout.notes: Precision is TP/(TP+FP), recall is TP/(TP+FN), and FPR is FP/all labelled normal inputs. Positive abstentions count as missed positives; unanswered normal cases are not silently counted as true negatives. Coverage is always shown when incomplete. AP and AUROC require genuine continuous scores, supplied only for CLIP; no ranking metric is invented for hard VLM labels. Unattended test prevalence is 242/962 = 25.2%, a useful AP reference. Positive-only weak candidate sets have no event precision or FPR; only target-prediction rates and response coverage are reported. The person-presence task has genuine person annotations but no absent-person controls. Source/camera bootstrap uses 2,000 draws, with only two unattended test families. Raw predictions were reloaded and all 40 saved metric summaries matched recomputation exactly.

layout.title: MiniCPM has the highest raw frame F1
layout.notes: All rows are raw categorical decisions on the same 962 inputs. MiniCPM has TP84 FP25 FN158 TN695: precision 77.1%, recall 34.7%, F1 .479 and FPR 3.47%. Its earlier constant-normal answer does not persist on this broader sample, but it still misses nearly two thirds of positives. MobileCLIP has 75.2% recall at 74.6% FPR; SmolVLM has 63.6% recall at 93.8% FPR. SigLIP has zero categorical recall with 2.64% FPR, while its continuous scores have AUROC .675 and AP .309. Positive prevalence is .252. All frame-test models have 100% response coverage. This is a descriptive provisional-label result, not a statistically established model winner or deployment validation.

layout.title: More temporal context has mixed effects
layout.notes: The 20-second window test uses the same endpoint labels as the frame study. MiniCPM recall falls from 34.7% to 10.7%, and FPR falls from 3.47% to .14%, with 26TP1FP216FN719TN. SmolVLM recall rises to 96.3% with 97.4% FPR; 14 unanswered inputs give 98.54% coverage. MobileCLIP recall is 76.0% with 68.5% FPR. SigLIP raw recall is only 1.65%, but window scores have AP .325 and AUROC .663. The earlier contact sheets used six seconds, so these results combine data expansion and changed temporal context. Contact sheets also reduce spatial resolution per frame. This experiment does not establish native video capability.

layout.title: Development false-alarm budgets transfer poorly
layout.notes: CLIP operating points are fitted using only development data. All eight rows are shown, including maximum-development-F1 and empirical 5% development-FPR budget selections. The latter is not a population guarantee. MobileCLIP budget-test FPR rises to 20.3% for frames and 35.1% for windows. SigLIP's window budget gives 7.0% recall at 5.14% FPR, while maximum-dev-F1 gives 55.4% recall at 30% FPR. MobileCLIP's maximum-dev-F1 frame threshold predicts every test endpoint anomalous, with F1 .402 simply reflecting prevalence. Test labels were not used to refit thresholds. Small held-out camera count limits claims about transfer.

items.value: Thresholds fitted on 553 normal + 255 positive development endpoints; frozen for test
An empirical 5% development constraint does not ensure 5% false positives on another camera.

layout.title: Detecting an interval can still mean many alarms
layout.notes: The screen groups the held-out predictions by source recording and ground-truth label and counts any raw categorical alarm. There are five positive source intervals and seven normal source intervals. This is not a streaming detector: no persistence filter, no event delay, and no alerts/hour estimate. Any-alarm counts are sensitive to interval length. MobileCLIP/SmolVLM frame predictions touch all five positive intervals but also all seven normal intervals. MiniCPM frame predictions touch three positive and three normal intervals; its window predictions touch four positive intervals and one normal interval, despite lower endpoint recall. Endpoint coverage and interval coverage therefore answer different questions. Source intervals are still clustered in only two camera families.

layout.title: The remaining datasets are usable as diagnostics
layout.notes: Each value is the number of target answers divided by all candidate inputs, including unanswered inputs. No verified anomaly recall or event precision/FPR is claimed. Littering provides 6,667 generic action-labelled candidates, some augmented; boxes can describe dropping, dumping, placing, throwing or tossing rather than rubbish disposal. Loitering provides 1,675 person-labelled images, without verified duration. Rough sleeping uses 111 synthetic lying/fall scenes without established public sleeping or bedding evidence. Low loitering/rough-sleeping rates may reflect correct rejection of insufficient evidence. High rates, such as SigLIP's rough-sleeping 95.5%, do not validate event recognition. SmolVLM abstains on 924 littering, 319 loitering and 13 rough-sleeping candidates. MiniCPM abstains on 24 rough-sleeping candidates.

layout.title: Seeing a person does not establish loitering
layout.notes: This separate grounding diagnostic uses the actual person boxes as person-presence evidence. It is positive-only, so it estimates positive hit rate, not precision or false-positive rate. The original loitering definition remains unchanged and requires duration evidence absent in the static export. SmolVLM detects person presence on 92.7% and answers loitering on .12%; MiniCPM detects person presence on 96.1% and answers loitering on 4.60%. The gap does not demonstrate loitering failure. SigLIP answers person presence on 17.4% and loitering on 84.5%, exposing strong definition/decision sensitivity without determining which unverified loitering labels are correct. There are no absent-person controls, and camera provenance is uncertain. Person and loitering images are the same inputs, not additional independent data.

layout.title: Oracle crops identify a promising component
layout.notes: The diagnostic supplies source bounding boxes free of charge and asks lying versus standing, not rough sleeping. Source-image grouping keeps mixed scenes together across splits. There are 111 lying and ten standing crops overall, with 67/6 in dev and 44/4 in test. SigLIP is correct on all 48 test crops. MiniCPM finds 40/44 lying crops and all four standing controls, F1 .952; it abstains on four positive crops. SmolVLM finds 26/44 lying crops and all standing controls, F1 .743; it abstains on 18 positive crops. MobileCLIP finds seven lying crops and incorrectly labels all four standing crops lying, F1 .255. Four negative controls are insufficient for a stable false-positive estimate. Oracle posture success is not validation of rough sleeping or of a deployed detector/crop pipeline.

layout.title: Smoking remains a difficult task
layout.notes: The prior smoking comparison already uses all 3,278 development frames, 1,422 positive and 1,856 normal, across 16 known groups. Raw smoking recall is .56% MobileCLIP, zero SigLIP, 5.41% SmolVLM and zero MiniCPM. The smoking source groups were historically inspected, so this is development evidence, not a fresh held-out test. VadCLIP is a separately trained supervised offline adaptation with future/full-sequence context and different training/test inputs. Its source split has nine train, four dev and three test sessions; test has 1,056 frames, 560 positive and 496 normal. The dev-selected dual_mean branch has AP .633, AUROC .587, recall 51.8%, F1 .565 and FPR 35.7%. The visual/dual_max branches predict all positive; a higher F1 from that trivial pattern is not better ranking. Neither protocol is pooled with unattended/proxy results, and VadCLIP is not evaluated for the other anomalies. No smoking or VadCLIP rerun was needed for this expansion.

layout.title: Choose the next experiment by failure mode
layout.notes: MiniCPM is worth pursuing for conservative unattended frame decisions, but misses many positives and its window endpoint recall drops. SigLIP has good oracle pose discrimination and some unattended score ranking, yet raw event decisions and frozen thresholds transfer poorly. MobileCLIP's high unattended FPR and poor oracle standing discrimination require label/prompt/crop development checks before deployment evaluation. SmolVLM's near-universal unattended window alarms and response abstentions are material issues. Across all new inputs, SmolVLM has 1,457 abstentions (10.6%) and MiniCPM has 45 (.33%); there are zero runtime errors. The next evidence should independently verify the provisional intervals, add deployment-domain cameras with real target events and matched negatives, and test detector plus crops/native temporal inputs under a frozen protocol. Repeated inspection means these test sources become development data for future tuning; a fresh source holdout is needed after changes. Do not infer deployment robustness from weak prediction rates or perfect four-negative pose results.
